      "nets": ["NET0212", "Net-(D1-K2)"],
      "observed": "The second LED of dual LED D1 has its anode (D1 pin 4, A2) on NET0212, which is also driven by U14 Y. Its cathode (D1 pin 2, K2) goes only through R2 to NET0212, so the LED's anode and its series resistor's far end sit on the same node. The LED has no voltage across it and cannot conduct. The other LED, D1 K1, correctly returns through R54 to GND.",
      "expected": "The series resistor R2 should return to GND, as R54 does for the K1 channel, so that current flows from U14 Y through A2 and K2 to ground.",

        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"R2\") (pin \"2\") (pintype \"passive\"))"},
        {"source": "spice", "quote": "R2 Net-_D1-K2_ NET0212 130"}
      ],
      "impact": "The status LED channel driven by U14 never lights, and the 130 ohm resistor simply loads the U14 output line that also goes to CAN connector pin 6 on J2 and J31.",
      "confidence": 0.5
    },
    {
      "category": "open_connection",
      "components": ["D15", "D34", "D39"],
      "pins": ["D15.2", "D34.2", "D39.2"],
      "nets": ["NET0058"],
      "observed": "The anodes of three indicator LEDs (green D15, green D34, yellow D39) sit on NET0058, and no other pin is connected to that net. The cathodes are driven through series resistors from Ethernet nLED and open-drain status outputs, so the LEDs are active-low and need their anodes at +3V3.",
      "expected": "The common anode net should be tied to +3V3, as is done for the similar LED D31 (anode on +3V3) and D44/D48 (anodes via resistors to +3V3).",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"18\") (name \"/NET0058\") (class \"Default\") (node (ref \"D15\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\") (pintype \"passive\")) (node (ref \"D34\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\") (pintype \"passive\")) (node (ref \"D39\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\") (pintype \"passive\")))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"D31\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\") (pintype \"passive\"))"}
      ],
      "impact": "Three status LEDs (Ethernet link/activity indicators and the PI activity LED path) never light, because their anodes have no supply connection.",
      "confidence": 0.35
    }
  ],
  "summary": "Two candidate faults stand out: the second channel of dual LED D1 is bypassed by R2, which returns to its own anode net instead of GND, and three indicator LED anodes on NET0058 have no supply connection. Both are visible in the netlist and are the most likely deviations from intent."
}

anomalies.observed: The second LED of dual LED D1 has its anode (D1 pin 4, A2) on NET0212, which is also driven by U14 Y. Its cathode (D1 pin 2, K2) goes only through R2 to NET0212, so the LED's anode and its series resistor's far end sit on the same node. The LED has no voltage across it and cannot conduct. The other LED, D1 K1, correctly returns through R54 to GND.
anomalies.expected: The series resistor R2 should return to GND, as R54 does for the K1 channel, so that current flows from U14 Y through A2 and K2 to ground.
anomalies.impact: The status LED channel driven by U14 never lights, and the 130 ohm resistor simply loads the U14 output line that also goes to CAN connector pin 6 on J2 and J31.

anomalies.observed: The anodes of three indicator LEDs (green D15, green D34, yellow D39) sit on NET0058, and no other pin is connected to that net. The cathodes are driven through series resistors from Ethernet nLED and open-drain status outputs, so the LEDs are active-low and need their anodes at +3V3.
anomalies.expected: The common anode net should be tied to +3V3, as is done for the similar LED D31 (anode on +3V3) and D44/D48 (anodes via resistors to +3V3).
anomalies.impact: Three status LEDs (Ethernet link/activity indicators and the PI activity LED path) never light, because their anodes have no supply connection.
